senses.gloss: m. (עָבַר) passer-by, transient. מום ע׳, v. עָבַר.
units: Snh. 70ᵃ דרש ע׳ גלילאה a Galilean travelling lecturer preached; Ḥull. 27ᵇ; (Sabb. 88ᵃ ההוא גלילאה).—Mostly ע׳ וָשָׁב traveller.—Pl. עוֹבְרִים, עוֹבְרִין.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 3:1:2">Y. Shebi. III, beg. 34ᶜ</cite> <he>לא חשו לע׳ ושָׁבִין וכ׳</he> they cared not for eventual travellers (who might misconstrue the act); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 103b:14">Snh. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>מפני שפיתו מצויה לעוֹבְרֵי דרכים</he> because his bread was ready for travellers, i.e. he was hospitable.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 109a:12">Ib. 109ᵃ</cite> <he>למה לנו עוברי דרכים וכ׳</he> why should we admit those travelling merchants who come only to take away our money?; Tanḥ.
